Article Title: Iran planning ‘multi-front’ attack on Israel with Hezbollah, Hamas, Houthis: Report
Article Text: Iran is reportedly seeking to bring its regional allies together for a coordinated assault on Israel, resembling the Hamas-led October 7 attack in 2023.Tehran wants to combine its own forces with Hezbollah in Lebanon, Hamas, the Houthis in Yemen and pro-Iranian militias in Iraq in a single campaign, the Jerusalem Post reported, citing Israeli assessments.The plan under consideration is intended to enable several fronts to operate against Israel at the same time, making a multi-front campaign part of the strategy from the outset.A report published last month said the IDF had identified renewed coordination between Hamas and Hezbollah with Iranian assistance, as part of an effort to increase pressure on Israel simultaneously from the North and South.According to a published IDF assessment cited by JPost, Hamas and Hezbollah had already begun coordinating an increase in their activities in recent weeks with Iranian assistance.Recent reports have also alleged that senior Quds Force officials held talks with commanders in Hezbollah, the Houthis and Iraqi militias regarding an expansion of the confrontation.Two senior officers in the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps claimed that during an earlier period of calm, senior Quds Force officials held conference calls with commanders from the three fronts, while Iranian advisers also worked with them on the ground, Jerusalem Post reported.During the same period, reports also emerged of Iranian efforts to accelerate the production of missiles and drones and restore capabilities that had been damaged.The rebuilding effort comes as the balance of power within the axis is also shifting. According to assessments, the damage inflicted on Hezbollah and the fall of the Assad regime in Syria have increased the importance of militias in Iraq and the Houthis in Yemen.At the same time, joint training exercises have been recorded, operational and personal ties have tightened, and coordination over political and military decisions among the components of the axis has increased.On October 7, Hamas launched its attack without the other fronts opening simultaneously and under full coordination.The idea of a broader regional war against Israel had emerged even earlier. Internal Hamas documents seized in the Gaza Strip after the attack indicated that Yahya Sinwar had sought to expand the confrontation and draw additional arenas into it.One of the planning documents stressed the need to "connect and prepare the external fronts", namely Lebanon, Syria and Sinai, as well as to agree in advance on communications mechanisms for both routine periods and wartime.However, this ambition had not been matched by full coordination ahead of the attack. According to published US and Israeli assessments, Iran and Hezbollah had not been informed in advance of all the details of the October 7 plan or the precise date on which it would be carried out.According to that assessment, Sinwar believed the success of the initial attack would subsequently draw Hezbollah and Iran into a broader campaign.Hezbollah opened fire in the North, but it did not launch a large-scale attack that same morning in parallel with Hamas' assault.According to reports in Arab media, Tehran is now allegedly seeking to address that gap precisely. The plan under consideration is intended to enable several fronts to operate against Israel at the same time, making a multi-front campaign part of the strategy from the outset.Khalil al-Hayya, who was elected Hamas' overall leader in July, is considered to have good relations with Iran and has for years been one of the organisation's central figures in maintaining ties with Tehran.Al-Hayya, a member of Hamas' Gaza-based camp who was close to Sinwar, strengthens within the organisation's leadership the faction seeking to preserve its close strategic relationship with Iran.
Article Summary: Tehran wants to combine its own forces with Hezbollah in Lebanon, Hamas, the Houthis in Yemen and pro-Iranian militias in Iraq. The plan under consideration is intended to enable several fronts to operate against Israel at the same time, making a multi-front campaign part of the strategy.

Article Title: Frozen like Pompeii, Ujjain’s 42 twisted skeletons await answers
Article Text:
42 skeletons unearthed at Kumhar Tekri in Ujjain await modern scientific analysis

DNA tests may solve the skeletons mystery





BHOPAL: Face down. On their backs. Seated. Twisted. Legs raised and folded. Children and adults. Males and females. Some buried, others cremated.Imagine Pompeii without its volcano, bodies caught in curious positions, a vanished community leaving behind fragments of their final rites on a hillock in western Madhya Pradesh.At Kumhar Tekri in Ujjain, 42 skeletons unearthed nearly nine decades ago are waiting for answers.Who were these people? Why were they buried in such strikingly different positions? Were they from different communities? Shell jewellery, urns containing ashes and bones, cups and dishes lay among the remains, adding more pieces to an archaeological puzzle that began in 1938-39 and may now get a fresh turn.The skeletons, unearthed during a trial excavation by Gwalior State's archaeological department during British rule, are believed to date to around the 3rd century BC, though an earlier date has not been ruled out.The better-preserved remains were sent for anthropological examination after the excavation and are now with ASI in Kolkata.ASI's regional office recently sought permission from its headquarters to dig adjoining Vaishya Tekri, about 2km from Kumhar Tekri or Potters' Hill.The site is home to a stupa nearly three times the diameter of the Sanchi stupa, and archaeologists believe it could supply missing context to the burials.Veena Mushrif-Tripathy, associate professor of biological anthropology at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute in Pune, who worked on the material in 2007-08, recommends re-examining the remains using modern methods such as AMS (advanced radiocarbon) dating, DNA analysis, and isotope studies to clarify age, sex, ancestry, and diet.Further study of their distinct morphological features and shell jewellery could also test the original excavators’ theory that the site belonged to a separate community.“It is difficult to confirm cultural identity just from burial positions, most probably, these were people from different groups or communities,” she said, adding that burials and cremations at the same site support the possibility.ASI’s Bhopal circle superintending archaeologist Dr Shivakant Bajpai said excavation at Vaishya Tekri could place Kumhar Tekri’s skeletons in a wider archaeological context and help investigators understand who they were.
Article Summary: 42 skeletons unearthed nearly nine decades ago are waiting for answers. Shell jewellery, urns containing ashes and bones, cups and dishes lay among the remains. Archaeologists believe they date to around the 3rd century BC, though an earlier date has not been ruled out. Modern methods such as AMS dating, DNA analysis, and isotope studies to clarify age, sex, ancestry, and diet.

Article Title: Revenue minister Ponguleti’s Paigah land registration plan hits CMO roadblock
Article Text:
The revenue minister's initiative to allow Paigah land registrations encounters pushback from the Chief Minister's Office (CMO)

TOI





HYDERABAD: A proposal by revenue minister Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy to allow registrations in disputed Paigah lands has run into resistance from the chief minister’s office (CMO).The disagreement centres on Paigah lands covered under civic suits (CS) 14 and CS 7 of 1958, spread across nearly 1,500 acres, mostly in the erstwhile Greater Hyderabad region. Hundreds of residential colonies, gated communities and high-rise apartment complexes have come up on these lands over the years, particularly in prime western suburbs such as Hafeezpet, Madhapur, Miyapur and surrounding areas, even as the legal battle between the state and private parties has continued for nearly six decades.A couple of weeks ago, Srinivas Reddy announced that the govt was considering permitting registrations in Paigah lands through conditional registrations. Under the proposal, registration documents would clearly state that the transactions would remain subject to the outcome of pending cases before the Supreme Court and high court.Officials point out that the state has lost several cases relating to these lands, including in the Supreme Court.Even if registrations were allowed, the lands would continue to remain on the 22-A prohibited properties list.However, despite the minister’s announcement, revenue principal secretary DS Lokesh Kumar has not issued any instructions to district collectors or the registration department. Sources said some collectors sought clarification from the govt on whether registrations could be permitted.Subsequently, the revenue department reportedly informed officials that no final decision had been taken, and that cases should be examined individually. The CMO is reportedly of the view that allowing registrations could be perceived as the govt conceding defeat in the long-running legal dispute.“The revenue department is of the opinion that GHMC had permitted the buildings including some high-rises with court orders and some registrations had taken place with the court orders. Now, there is no point in stopping them for further registrations,” a senior revenue official said.For instance Mahindra Ashvita Cooperative Housing Society in survey No. 78/2 of Hafeezpet has around 664 flats. Residents say the project obtained building permission in 2015, received an occupancy certificate from GHMC in 2018 and has been occupied ever since. They also point out that property taxes have been paid regularly over the years.“The state govt put our land and apartments in 22-A claiming it as CS 14 land and stopped registrations from Nov 2025. As the building is in 22-A, we are unable to sell our flats for children’s education, weddings and even obtain loans on the flats,” an office-bearer of the Mahindra Ashvita society toldHe said the residents’ association has submitted nearly 90 representations to various authorities over the past few months, but the issue remains unresolved.In Hafeezpet there are about 700 acres Paigah lands in survey no 77 to 80 of Hafeezpet, where there is a dispute between the state govt and private parties, around 430 acres of 484 acres in survey no 80 in Hafeezpet are covered by the buildings including gated communities and apartments. In survey nos 77 to 80, of Hafeezpet village decrees confirmed up to Supreme Court, but they are still under prohibition. In survey no 80, there are 484 acres of that only 50 acres are vacant, and the constructions have come up in the remaining land and residential colonies have come up.Similarly in survey no 172 of Hydernagar village near Kukatpally, of the 192 acres, the SC in June 2023, except 54 acres (under OSA No 55 of 2004), asked the private parties to establish the ownership afresh. In Ghansimiyaguda near Shamshabad, S No 3 and 4, they are continuing under encroachments, but the govt failed to protect the lands.
Article Summary: The disagreement centres on Paigah lands covered under civic suits (CS) 14 and CS 7 of 1958, spread across nearly 1,500 acres, mostly in the erstwhile Greater Hyderabad region. Hundreds of residential colonies, gated communities and high- rise apartment complexes have come up on these lands.

Article Title: 'Don't stoop so low': CJP activist reacts to complaint over 'objectionable' remarks on Hindu deities
Article Text:
CJP activist outside Delhi's Parliament Street Police Station

(With inputs from ANI)

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think of the advocates' actions to file a police complaint? Justified and essential. Overreacting and unnecessary. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion





NEW DELHI: A CJP activist has hit back at two advocates who filed police complaints against her and her father over alleged objectionable remarks about Hindu deities on social media.Reacting to the complaints, the CJP activist told news agency ANI, "They are raising illegal demands about sending my father to jail. Don't stoop so low."The two advocates approached the police after alleging that the CJP activist and her father had made objectionable remarks about Hindu deities in social media posts.Advocate Amita Sachdeva said she came across old posts by the CJP activist on X in which she allegedly used the word “vaishya” for Goddess Durga and mocked Goddess Saraswati."Yesterday I came across some tweets posted by her on 'X'. They were old tweets. She used the word vaishya for goddess Maa Durga; she mocked goddess Saraswati. So yesterday I gave her a warning and asked her politely to delete these posts. You cannot insult my gods. If you want to believe them, it's your choice," Sachdeva told ANI.Sachdeva said she had given the CJP activist and her father time until 1pm on Saturday to remove the posts, but they did not do so."We will not allow that. So I gave her time till 1 p.m (on Saturday), but they didn't do that. Neither she nor her father. Then I was constrained to file the complaint, which I did. And police have assured us that they will take necessary steps," she said.Another advocate, Anurag Gupta, also filed a complaint against the duo."We went inside to file a complaint against CJP activist and her father. Our grievance is that people have started mocking Hindus and hurling abuse at our gods and goddesses. I want to ask the youth and all Hindus across the country: what kind of stupor are you in to tolerate this?""If everyone across India were to wake up and start filing complaints, these foul-mouthed individuals would automatically stop, because right now, they have lost all fear of consequences," Gupta said."The SHO said he would register the complaint and initiate further action. If the SHO fails to file the complaint, we will take the matter to the DC; if the DC doesn't act either, we will approach the Supreme Court directly," Gupta told ANI outside Sansad Marg Police Station.Meanwhile, advocate Prateek Jha submitted a separate representation at Parliament Street Police Station on Saturday, alleging “double standards” in the way Delhi Police handled protests by different groups at Jantar Mantar.Jha referred to an incident on July 21, 2026, when a group had gathered and blocked Jantar Mantar. He alleged that police personnel faced “many atrocities” during the incident and said he had raised concerns over what he described as a violation of constitutional principles.He further alleged that when another group later arrived at the site to protest, Delhi Police made them leave and did not allow them to continue their gathering.Jha said a copy of his representation was submitted to the SHO, although he claimed it was not stamped as received.“If not, we will move to court,” Jha said.The representation comes amid police action against Swatantra Bhardwaj, who was arrested in connection with an assault case during CJP's Janatar Mantar protest in Delhi.
Article Summary: Advocate Amita Sachdeva said she came across old posts by the CJP activist on X in which she allegedly used the word “vaishya” for Goddess Durga and mocked Goddess Saraswati. She said she had given the activist and her father time until 1pm on Saturday to remove the posts, but they did not do so.

Article Title: Ahmedabad, Surat courts receive bomb threat emails
Article Text:
File photo, image enhanced with AI





AHMEDABAD: Courts in Gujarat, including the Surat district court and courts in Ahmedabad, received emails threatening bomb attacks on Saturday, following which police and security agencies conducted security checks.The Surat district court received an email threatening to blow up the premises with a bomb.After the threat was received, bomb disposal squad personnel and police teams reached the court and carried out security checks.The lawyers' association, however, raised concerns over repeated bomb threat emails being received by the court and alleged that the premises were not evacuated despite the threat."Even after receiving the bomb threat mail, the police have not vacated the court premises, and work is continuing. The accused are not being caught and are directly targeting the justice system," said Bhavesh Rabari, member, Bar Council of Gujarat.Earlier, courts in Ahmedabad had also received an email warning of a possible attack. The email reportedly carried the message, "Court on alert", following which security agencies were alerted.Ahmedabad Police said routine procedures were being followed in connection with the threat and that further investigation was underway.(With inputs from ANI)
Article Summary: Surat district court received an email threatening to blow up the premises with a bomb. The lawyers' association, however, raised concerns over repeated bomb threat emails being received by the court. The email reportedly carried the message, "Court on alert", following which security agencies were alerted.

Article Title: ‘Uncle is bad’: 5-year-old’s remark helps family uncover 'rape' in Jaipur
Article Text:
A tragic case emerged from Jaipur involving the alleged assault of a 5-year-old girl by someone known to her family (Representative image)





JAIPUR: A five-year-old girl’s remark that a family acquaintance was “bad” led her family to discover that she had allegedly been raped by him about 15 days ago, following which the accused fled and was arrested from Ramdevra in Jaisalmer, police said on Saturday.The accused, who was known to the family, was arrested after the girl’s grandmother filed a complaint. He was produced before a court on Friday and sent to judicial custody.According to police, the incident occurred around 15 days ago when the accused allegedly assaulted the child after finding her alone.The girl did not tell anyone about the incident as the accused had allegedly threatened to kill her if she disclosed it, news agency PTI reported.Three days ago, the accused came to the family’s house on the pretext of meeting them. The girl was playing with her grandmother when she saw him and remarked, “Uncle is bad.”Police said the grandmother initially dismissed the comment as an innocent remark by a child.The accused allegedly became suspicious that the girl might have revealed something and questioned her about the remark.After he left the house, the girl told her family what had allegedly happened to her.The family then approached the police and lodged a complaint.Police said the accused fled from his home after learning about the complaint.A police team formed under provisions of the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act tracked the accused to Ramdevra in Jaisalmer district and arrested him.He was subsequently produced before a court and sent to judicial custody, police said.(With agency inputs)(The victim's identity has not been revealed to protect her privacy as per Supreme court directives on cases related to sexual assault)
Article Summary: A five-year-old girl's remark that a family acquaintance was "bad" led her family to discover that she had allegedly been raped by him. The accused, who was known to the family, was arrested after the girl’s grandmother filed a complaint. The incident occurred around 15 days ago when the accused allegedly assaulted the child after finding her alone.

Article Title: Jilted lover abducts girl's minor brother, drinks poison during 22-km police chase in Delhi
Article Text:
Officials said the accused, Dharam Pal, a resident of Kasganj district in Uttar Pradesh, was immediately shifted to BJRM Hospital, where he remains in custody.





NEW DELHI: A jilted lover who abducted a girl's 11-year-old brother and threatened to kill him unless she married him was hospitalised after consuming poison during a 22-kilometre police chase here when cops were about to arrest him, police said on Saturday.Officials said the accused, Dharam Pal, a resident of Kasganj district in Uttar Pradesh, was immediately shifted to BJRM Hospital, where he remains in custody.The boy had left home for school on August 31 but did not return. Police said he was rescued from Azadpur Flyover on Friday after they chased the accused from Loni in Ghaziabad to Delhi, covering a distance of about 22 kilometres. The accused was fleeing by bus, police said.According to police, Pal wanted to marry the boy's sister and live with her, but she was unwilling to maintain any relationship with him.Police said the accused allegedly kidnapped her younger brother to pressure the family.He then called the boy's mother from an unknown number, identified himself and threatened to kill the child if his demand that the girl be sent to him was not fulfilled.The Jahangir Puri police station received a PCR call regarding the boy's disappearance on August 31 and registered an FIR based on the family's complaint.Officials said police developed leads regarding their movements through technical surveillance and field investigation and tracked them to Loni in Ghaziabad.(With inputs from PTI)
Article Summary: Dharam Pal, a resident of Kasganj district in Uttar Pradesh, was immediately shifted to BJRM Hospital, where he remains in custody. The boy had left home for school on August 31 but did not return. Pal wanted to marry the boy's sister and live with her, but she was unwilling to maintain any relationship with him.

Article Title: Guri Chahal rape case: Survivor opposes police cancellation report
Article Text:
FIR registered at Sohana police station on May 1 (Representative Image)





MOHALI: The rape survivor in the high-profile case involving Guri Chahal has opposed the cancellation report filed by the police, alleging that she was not contacted during the investigation despite directions from the court.The survivor appeared before the Mohali court on Saturday along with her counsel, advocate H.S. Dhanoa, and recorded her statement.During the proceedings, she expressed dissatisfaction with the police investigation and told the court that she had full faith in the law and the judicial system and would pursue the matter through legal means.According to Dhanoa, an FIR was registered at Sohana police station on May 1, 2026. He said the police subsequently filed an application seeking cancellation of the case before the court on July 24.Dhanoa alleged that during the proceedings, the court had directed Mohali police officials to produce the survivor before it.However, he alleged that the police did not contact her regarding the court's direction, following which she appeared in court herself along with her lawyers.The counsel said the survivor recorded her statement before the court and opposed the police cancellation report.She reportedly told the court that she was not satisfied with the investigation and wanted to pursue the matter in accordance with the law.Dhanoa said the survivor had urged the court to consider all the facts and circumstances of the case, along with the manner in which the investigation was conducted, before taking a decision on the cancellation report.He added that he had not yet received the complete set of documents relating to the cancellation report submitted by the police. Once the documents are made available, he said, he would examine them in detail and place the survivor's objections and legal submissions before the court.The court will now consider the police cancellation report, the survivor's statement and her objections before deciding whether to accept the report or order further proceedings in the matter.
Article Summary: The rape survivor in the high-profile case involving Guri Chahal has opposed the cancellation report filed by the police. The survivor appeared before the Mohali court on Saturday along with her counsel, advocate H.S. Dhanoa, and recorded her statement.

Article Title: Hyderabad airport road accident: 33-year-old woman dead as car rams bike from behind
Article Text:
A 33-year-old woman, Pullamoni Radhika, died after a car hit her motorcycle





HYDERABAD: A 33-year-old woman, Pullamoni Radhika, died after the bike she was travelling on as a pillion rider was hit by a car from behind on the Shamshabad Airport Approach Road near the ROB U-Turn early Saturday morning.According to officials, the accident occurred around 6.43 am when Radhika and Prithviraj, both residents of Shamshabad, were travelling on a bike.The two were reportedly on their way to work at the airport when a car approached from behind.Police said the car, allegedly driven by a man identified as Uma Kant, hit the bike after the driver failed to notice a speed breaker on the road.The impact caused both occupants of the two-wheeler to fall, with Radhika sustaining severe injuries to her head and face.She was immediately shifted to a hospital, where doctors declared her brought dead. Prithviraj, who was riding the bike, also sustained injuries and was taken for treatment.Police said Uma Kant fled from the scene and is currently absconding. A team from the Rajiv Gandhi International Airport (RGIA) police station has been sent to trace him, the officials said.A case has been registered and further investigation is underway.
Article Summary: A 33-year-old woman, Pullamoni Radhika, died after the bike she was travelling on as a pillion rider was hit by a car from behind on the Shamshabad Airport Approach Road near the ROB U-Turn early Saturday morning. Police said the car, allegedly driven by a man identified as Uma Kant, hit the bike after the driver failed to notice a speed breaker.

Article Title: ‘Don’t give me these useless jumlas’: MP Kangana Ranaut pulls up officials over Rs 11 crore MPLADS funds
Article Text:
BJP MP Kangana Ranaut

(With Agency Inputs)





MANDI: BJP MP Kangana Ranaut pulled up officials during a DISHA Committee meeting in Himachal Pradesh over the alleged delay in implementing development works under the Members of Parliament Local Area Development Scheme (MPLADS), questioning the utilisation of nearly Rs 11 crore allocated for projects in her constituency.Kangana expressed anger over what she described as repeated assurances from officials that there were no problems with the utilisation of MPLADS funds."Don’t give me these useless jumlas (fake promises). I’m getting them at every Disha Committee meeting. Last time as well, when I inquired about MPLADS, and our DISHA committees meet so regularly, whenever I asked about MPLADS, I was told that there was absolutely no hiccup and that 90% of our money was on the ground. But what turned out to be the reality? The reality came to light only when external agencies conducted detailed surveys on this. .." she said."What I am trying to say is that I don't need your assurances to 'address' it—get the bloody job done now! The time for 'addressing' things is gone. Those are two-year-old matters. Those are one-and-a-half to two years old matters. Now get the job done and report to me that this is done!" she added.The BJP MP also questioned the utilisation of funds allocated for development works, saying nearly Rs 11 crore had been released while only a small portion had reportedly been spent. Reports said that in Mandi alone, around Rs 50-60 lakh had been utilised out of approximately Rs 5.5 crore.Ranaut further questioned the accountability and work ethic of officials, expressing concern over how she would explain the situation to the media and people of her constituency."What am I supposed to say before the media out there? That people come here only to draw their salaries? What am I supposed to say about the people of our state? What am I to say about their work ethic? That they are utterly lazy, utterly incompetent people occupying these chairs? Is that what I should say to the national media? About my own constituency? And about my own mountain people?..." she said.The MP directed officials to expedite the pending development works and report on their completion. Several projects have reportedly remained pending over issues including land availability and necessary permissions.
Article Summary: BJP MP Kangana Ranaut pulled up officials during a DISHA Committee meeting in Himachal Pradesh. She questioned the utilisation of nearly Rs 11 crore allocated for projects in her constituency. Several projects have reportedly remained pending over issues including land availability and necessary permissions.

Article Title: Ketan Agarwal murder: Friend of Chetan Choudhary held for conspiracy, custody till Sept 12
Article Text:
Pune police have arrested a 22-year-old man, Ritesh Hange, in connection with the murder of realtor Ketan Agarwal

Third arrest in Ketan Agarwal murder case

Alleged love triangle behind realtor's killing





PUNE: Pune Rural Police have arrested a 22-year-old man for allegedly being part of the conspiracy to kill realtor Ketan Agarwal at Lohagad Fort in June and secured his police custody till September 12, making him the third accused to be held in the case, officials said on SaturdayA Pune court has remanded him to police custody till September 12The arrested man, Ritesh Hange, is a friend of Chetan Choudhary, who police allege was in a relationship with Agarwal's fiancée, Siya Goyal.Police said Goyal, 20, and Choudhary, 22, allegedly pushed Agarwal off a cliff at Lohagad Fort in Pune district on June 18, resulting in his death."During the investigation, it came to light that Ritesh was involved in the planning of Ketan Agarwal's murder," Pune Rural superintendent of police Sandip Singh Gill said.Hange has been arrested for his alleged role in the murder conspiracy, he said.Another police officer said Hange had been involved in planning the murder along with Choudhary and Goyal."He was aware of the earlier plan of Goyal and Chaudhary to injure Ketan by breaking his hands and legs and subsequently eliminate him. After allegedly executing the murder at Lohagad fort on June 18, Chetan contacted Ritesh and informed him about it," the officer said.Police said Hange was aware of the earlier plan to attack Agarwal before the alleged killing.According to police, Agarwal and Goyal had got engaged in February, while she was allegedly in a relationship with Choudhary.Investigators allege that Goyal and Choudhary planned to eliminate Agarwal as they considered him an obstacle in their relationship.Hange is the third person arrested in the case after Choudhary and Goyal.(With PTI inputs)
Article Summary: Pune police have arrested a 22-year-old man, Ritesh Hange, in connection with the murder of realtor Ketan Agarwal. Hange is a friend of Chetan Choudhary, who police allege was in a relationship withAgarwal's fiancée, Siya Goyal. Goyal, 20, and ChoudHary, 22, allegedly pushed AgarWal off a cliff at Lohagad Fort in Pune district on June 18, resulting in his death.

Article Title: Not given FIR copy, says ex-bureaucrat Ashish Joshi; no need at this stage, say cops
Article Text:
Ex-bureaucrat Ashish Joshi





NEW DELHI: Former bureaucrat Ashish Joshi , who was questioned by Delhi Police 's special cell for several hours Wednesday, said he and his lawyers were yet to be pro-vided with a copy of the FIR against him.Speaking to TOI, Joshi, a 1992-batch officer of the Indian Post and Telecommunication Accounts and Finance Service, said he went to Delhi Police headquarters Thursday with a letter from his lawyers asking that he be provided with a copy of the FIR against him. The FIR has been registered under section 192 of Bharatiya Nyay Sanhita, which relates to "wantonly giving provocation with intent to cause riot".Joshi said he was approached by two Delhi Police officers as he was leaving Nehru Park Wednesday morning."They showed me the first page of the FIR for a short while. It mentioned a post I had made on X on Aug 26 about SIR and elections in West Bengal. I was not shown the second page of the FIR; so, I am at the police headquarters with a letter from my lawyers to seek a copy, which they are required to provide to me," Joshi said.Police sources said as Joshi was not arrested and only questioned, there was no need to provide a copy of the FIR at this stage.Sources said that the cops questioned him regarding his post on X that called for "Nuremberg style trial" - military tribunals held after World War II - of the chief election commission in connection with the West Bengal elections while demanding that they be held again.During questioning, Joshi claimed, he was asked about his social media activity, including his post on the chief election commissioner and another he made on Aug 13.Earlier in the day, Joshi posted on X that he was not allowed to inform his family and friends that he was being questioned by police offi-cials Wednesday."Informing an individual's family during interrogation or detention is a legal mandate, not an optional courtesy... I was only permitted to make a call at 6.38pm, leaving my family & friends in total panic the entire day," he posted on X, tagging Delhi Police commissioner Anurag Kumar.Delhi Police, however, rejected the allegations, asserting that all mandated legal provisions were followed during the questioning. Police said that following their request to join the investigation, Joshi came to the special cell's office in New Friends Colony in his own vehicle and was escorted home safely and cordially in the evening.Sources in Delhi Police had said Wednesday that Joshi and his wife were duly informed about the questioning and the registration of an FIR.
Article Summary: Ex-bureaucrat Ashish Joshi was questioned by Delhi Police's special cell for several hours Wednesday. Joshi, a 1992-batch officer of the Indian Post and Telecommunication Accounts and Finance Service, said he and his lawyers were yet to be pro-vided with a copy of the FIR.

Article Title: ‘World has reached the moon, we still carry children’: 80-year wait for bridge in Chhattisgarh's Sonpal village
Article Text:
In Sonpal village, daily life is disrupted by the absence of a crucial bridge





RAIPUR: “The world has reached the moon, but we still carry our children on our shoulders across the stream to help them reach school.” That is how residents of remote Sonpal village in Durgukondal block of Kanker district describe an eight-decade wait for a bridge they say has been promised by successive governments but never built.For villagers, the missing bridge is not merely an infrastructure gap. During the rains, it determines whether children can reach school, whether families can travel for work or treatment, and whether anyone can cross the village boundary without risking a fall into the swollen stream.Videos of parents carrying children on their shoulders through the flooded crossing have surfaced on social media, drawing attention to the village’s daily struggle.One of the women said villagers had even travelled to the state capital with applications seeking a bridge, but nothing changed. “It feels as if we are still not part of independent India,” she said.“The four months of monsoon are the worst. If someone falls ill, an ambulance cannot reach us. Children miss school, and sometimes their books get washed away in the water,” she said. “How are our children supposed to go to school? If they have to attend, the only option is for parents to carry them on their shoulders, otherwise their uniforms get soaked and covered in mud.They fall and others are so short, they can't stand in that water. Who would understand our pain? A bridge has to be built here.”Village head Sanuram Dugga said generations have lived with the same demand. “Our fathers and grandfathers kept asking for this bridge and died waiting. Now our generation is asking for it,” he said. “Governments come and go— everyone said it would be built. The promises were made, not the bridge.”A 2.3km blacktop road, constructed about three years ago at a cost of crores, exists on both sides of the stream. But in between, the road gets inundated during the monsoon.During the monsoon, villagers say adults wade across at considerable risk, while younger children are carried on shoulders or backs to get them safely to the other side.Women in the village — Iswanti Rana, Subhadra Patel, Sagro Bai Dugga, Basanti Kumeti and Somari Yadav — said they have heard the same assurance since they got married in Sonpal: “The bridge will be built this year.” Now, their children are bearing the brunt.Residents say the absence of a crossing affects not only schoolchildren but anyone needing to reach markets, hospitals, workplaces or government offices outside the village.Mahendra Singh Thakur, a sub-engineer with the Bridge Corporation in Kanker, told reporters that the Sonpal bridge has been included in the 2026-27 budget and that a fresh estimate will now be prepared and forwarded for further action.For Sonpal, however, an estimate is still not a bridge.
Article Summary: In Sonpal village, daily life is disrupted by the absence of a crucial bridge. During the rains, it determines whether children can reach school, whether families can travel for work or treatment, and whether anyone can cross the village boundary without risking a fall into the swollen stream.

Article Title: 6 drug traffickers held in Lucknow with narcotic medicines worth Rs 1 crore
Article Text:
The arrests were made on Friday at Kanhaiya Pharma in Transport Nagar, Lucknow.





LUCKNOW: The Anti-Narcotics Task Force (ANTF) operational unit in Lucknow has arrested six active drug traffickers and recovered a large consignment of narcotic and psychotropic medicines, including codeine-based cough syrup, tramadol capsules, and alprazolam tablets, collectively valued at an estimated Rs 1 crore.The arrests were made on Friday at Kanhaiya Pharma in Transport Nagar, Lucknow.Kishan Vaswani, Sameer Ahmed, Shad Irshad, Umesh Kumar, Satendra Singh, and Vishal Chaurasia were arrested.According to the ANTF, the accused were found in possession of 720 bottles of 100-ml ONEREX cough syrup containing codeine, 1,20,000 SPASMONAM PLUS capsules containing Tramadol Hydrochloride, and 9,60,000 ALZOMAC-0.5 tablets containing Alprazolam.Besides the drugs, the team also recovered seven mobile phones and Rs 11,140 in cash from the suspects.A case has been registered at Sarojini Nagar police station in the Lucknow Commissionerate under Sections 8, 21, 22, and 29 of the Narcotic Drugs and Psychotropic Substances (NDPS) Act. Police said legal proceedings have been initiated against all six accused.During interrogation, the arrested suspects reportedly told investigators that they operated together to illegally procure and sell narcotic medicines for higher profits.They allegedly pooled money to purchase the medicines and subsequently delivered the consignments to different parties for monetary gain. The money earned from the transactions was then divided among the members of the group and used for their personal expenses and lifestyles, police said.Investigators said the questioning of the accused had yielded important information regarding the suspected drug network. The ANTF is now working on the forward and backward linkages of the case to identify the source from which the medicines were procured, the intended recipients of the consignment, and other persons associated with the network.Further investigation is underway to establish the complete supply chain and identify other individuals involved in the illegal trade.
Article Summary: The arrests were made on Friday at Kanhaiya Pharma in Transport Nagar, Lucknow. The suspects allegedly pooled money to purchase the medicines and delivered the consignments to different parties for monetary gain. The money earned from the transactions was then divided among the members of the group and used for their personal expenses.

Article Title: Konda Surekha tied rakhi to CM Revanth Reddy. Days later, he dropped her from his cabinet
Article Text:
Konda Surekha tied rakhi to CM Revanth Reddy

Controversy over daughter’s remarks

Surekha sacked from Cabinet





HYDERABAD: Days before minister Konda Surekha was sacked from the Cabinet, she was seen tying a rakhi to chief minister A Revanth Reddy at his residence, amid a controversy over remarks made by her daughter against the CM and the Congress party.In the video, Surekha, along with Women and Child Welfare Minister Seethakka, is seen tying a rakhi to Revanth Reddy during Raksha Bandhan celebrations.After the celebrations, Revanth posted on X: “On the occasion of Raksha Bandhan, which stands as a symbol of the bond between sisters and brothers, ministers Seethakka and Konda Surekha tied rakhis. I wish that this Raksha Bandhan festival brings joy to every girl child. #RakshaBandhan #Rakhi #Telangana.”In a separate post, he said: “To every elder sister, younger sister. People’s governance is Rakshabandhan. #RakshaBandhan #Rakhi #Telangana.”Speaking to reporters, Surekha said she had tied a rakhi to Revanth as she had done over the past two years.Asked about demands from Congress legislators for action against her, she said: “I do not want to comment on this auspicious festive day.”She added that she had prayed for the blessings of women to remain with Revanth.“Don’t single me out in this case. Today is a festival day and we all women have tied rakhis to the CM,” she said.The Raksha Bandhan celebrations came amid a controversy over remarks made by Surekha’s daughter, Konda Susmita, against Revanth and the Congress party.Susmita had criticised Revanth after he stated that sitting Parkal MLA Revuri Prakash Reddy would be given the Congress ticket from the constituency in the next Assembly election.A contender for the ticket herself, Susmita had said on August 19 that the CM did not have the authority to make such a decision and had also levelled other allegations against him.Surekha maintained that she could not be held responsible for her adult daughter’s comments. However, several Congress MLAs and MLCs demanded action against her.The TPCC disciplinary committee subsequently recommended action against Surekha for failing to condemn her daughter’s remarks.CM A Revanth Reddy later dropped Konda Surekha from his Cabinet, amid growing concerns over indiscipline within the state Congress.Sources told that the Congress high command had preferred Surekha to resign, but she refused to quit and travelled to Delhi to present her case before the party leadership.After meeting Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Surekha said she had explained her position and challenged the high command to take whatever action it deemed appropriate.She reiterated that her daughter was an adult and that her remarks should not be linked to her.Revanth had also taken up the matter with AICC general secretary (organisation) K C Venugopal in Delhi and sought action against Surekha. Venugopal’s refusal to meet Surekha had further fuelled speculation that disciplinary action was imminent.
Article Summary: Konda Surekha was seen tying a rakhi to chief minister A Revanth Reddy at his residence. The celebrations came amid a controversy over remarks made by her daughter, Konda Susmita, against Revanth and the Congress party.Surekha maintained that she could not be held responsible for her adult daughter's comments.
